works.title: Gated Delta Networks: Improving Mamba2 with Delta Rule
works.note: The trained-model ablation in Appendix A.2 reports worse average evaluation perplexity without the output gate, while the main model also adds a distinct recurrent forgetting gate, qualifying any general claim that gating only helps early rather than establishing or refuting the specific spiking WikiText-2 reversal [ref:6].

works.title: Gated Linear Attention Transformers with Hardware-Efficient Training
works.note: GLA reports benefits from data-dependent state decay but marginally better training perplexity after removing its beta gate, showing that gate placement matters, although these ablations measure training perplexity after a fixed token budget rather than converged validation generalization [ref:11].

works.title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
works.note: Language-model ablations at Chinchilla token budgets favor input-dependent selective state-space parameters and identify the gating-related delta parameter as especially important, but do not isolate a sigmoid output gate or demonstrate asymptotic convergence or the SNN ranking reversal [ref:17].

works.title: NAS-Bench-101: Towards Reproducible Neural Architecture Search
works.note: The benchmark attributes weak Hyperband and BOHB speedups to low rank correlation across training budgets and warns that intermediate checkpoints are learning-rate-schedule dependent, directly supporting caution about short-training architecture rankings, albeit on image classifiers rather than SNN language models [ref:41].

works.title: Efficient Global Neural Architecture Search
works.note: For 240 CIFAR-10 architectures, the paper reports only 0.65 Spearman correlation between one-epoch and fifty-epoch validation rankings, supporting the possibility that short-training search selects fast starters rather than the best longer-trained architecture [ref:36].

works.title: Hyperband: A Novel Bandit-Based Approach to Hyperparameter Optimization
works.id_or_venue: arXiv:1603.06560; Journal of Machine Learning Research 18(185):1-52
works.note: Hyperband explicitly discusses better eventual models having slower convergence and hedges early-stopping aggressiveness across resource-allocation brackets, supporting multi-fidelity confirmation while warning that uninformative low-resource performance can limit its benefit [ref:58].

works.title: Random Search and Reproducibility for Neural Architecture Search
works.note: The venue abstract reports competitive random-search-with-early-stopping results on Penn Treebank and CIFAR-10, qualifying the finding by showing that partial-training search can remain useful without establishing that early rankings reliably match final rankings (abstract-only evidence here) [ref:27].

works.title: Language Modeling with Gated Convolutional Networks
works.note: The paper reports faster convergence with gated linear units than tanh-based gates and overfitting of its gated convolutional model on small Penn Treebank, making the finding plausible while not isolating gating as the cause of overfitting or demonstrating an early-to-late ranking reversal [ref:45].

works.title: GLU Variants Improve Transformer
works.note: Parameter- and compute-matched GLU-family feed-forward layers improve held-out pretraining log-perplexity at both shorter and longer training budgets, qualifying any universal gate-overfitting explanation while providing a precedent for capacity-matched controls outside delta-rule models [ref:51].

output.summary: The general conclusion is expected: NAS and AutoML literature already documents unreliable early rankings and motivates multi-fidelity evaluation. Gated language models also provide precedents for faster optimization and small-data overfitting, but not proof that gates cause the latter. The potentially distinctive contribution is the controlled early-to-late reversal for a spiking DeltaNet output gate on WikiText-2, particularly against parameter-matched and built-in-gate controls. Existing Gated DeltaNet output-gate ablations instead show benefits after their training budget, so gate placement, parameterization, data scale, and training protocol matter. None of these sources establishes the exact SNN reversal; finite-budget results should not be equated with proven convergence, and multi-seed confirmation remains important.
